hints.junior: The docs said size="large" worked. It had been renamed to variant three months earlier and nobody updated the doc page.
hints.mid: A markdown doc is a second, independent copy of information the component's source already has, nothing keeps the two in sync.
hints.staff: Descriptions of code drift because updating them is a disconnected second step nothing in review flags as affected by a prop change.

hints.junior: Same renamed prop, two doc formats, toggle to see which one still shows the prop that no longer exists.
hints.mid: The markdown panel is frozen text someone has to remember to edit, the controls panel regenerates from real prop types every render.
hints.staff: The markdown version doesn't error, it just quietly shows a dead prop, that's the dangerous part, it looks confidently correct.

hints.junior: A Storybook story renders the real component, so its controls panel can't show a prop that doesn't exist anymore.
hints.mid: Controls are generated from the component's actual prop types, not from anything a human typed into a separate doc file.
hints.staff: A story is also a rendered instance, so visual regressions and interaction behavior are inspectable the same way prop shape is.

hints.junior: Storybook can't drift on prop shape, but written guidance text next to a story can still go stale the same way any prose can.
hints.mid: Require a story per exported component in CI, so a new component can't ship with zero live documentation.
hints.staff: Publish Storybook per-PR so reviewers see a prop change's actual doc impact in the same review, not as a deferred follow-up.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a documented prop that hadn't actually existed on the real component for three months.
sections.mid: A markdown doc describing a component's API is a second, independent copy of information the source code already contains — the moment either copy changes without the other, they disagree, and nothing enforces they stay in sync.
sections.staff: This is the general problem with documentation that describes code rather than rendering it — nothing in a normal PR review flags a docs file as affected by a prop rename, unless a human specifically remembers to check.

sections.junior: The fix is docs that render the real component, so the controls panel is generated from real prop types instead of hand typed text.
sections.mid: Storybook generates the controls panel from the component's actual prop types, not from anything a human typed into a separate file — a prop that no longer exists can't appear in the controls.
sections.staff: A story is also a rendered instance, so beyond prop-shape accuracy, a broken hover state or missing focus ring shows up by looking at the running story, not by reading a paragraph that claims the component is accessible.

sections.junior: Toggle between a hand written markdown doc and a live controls panel, both describing the same button after a prop rename.
sections.mid: The markdown doc's content is frozen text, someone has to remember to edit it. The controls panel is generated from the component's real prop types every time it renders.
sections.staff: The markdown version doesn't error or warn — it just quietly shows a prop that silently no longer does anything, which is the dangerous part.

sections.junior: A markdown doc describing your component's props will drift the moment the component changes. Render the real component instead, so the docs can't lie.
sections.mid: Storybook renders the real component with controls generated from its real prop types — the docs can't describe a prop that no longer exists.
sections.staff: Require a story per exported component in CI so a prop change's doc impact shows up in the same review, not as a deferred follow-up.
